title: Power Apps: responsive, multi-column starting layout for SharePoint list forms (preview)
summary: The layout details and environment-setting command are supported, and the roadmap fields match. However, the summary says administrators need no switch even though Microsoft has not documented how the template is enabled; the page also overstates its availability to anyone creating a new form.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The previous template used a mobile-sized canvas with a single-column form.
claims.quote: The previous template used a mobile-sized canvas with a single-column form.

claims.claim: The new template uses the Flexible canvas type and adapts to available space.
claims.quote: The new template uses the Flexible canvas type and a responsive layout that adapts to the available space.

claims.claim: Learn describes the template where it is enabled for new form creation.
claims.quote: This article describes the responsive template where it's enabled for new form creation.

claims.claim: Makers open a list and select Integrate > Power Apps > Customize forms.

Open your list in SharePoint or Microsoft Lists.

claims.claim: The generated form uses one column below app width 640.
claims.quote: Less than 640. | One.

claims.claim: The generated form uses two columns from app width 640 to below 900.

claims.claim: The generated form uses three columns at app width 900 or more.
claims.quote: 900 or more. | Three.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Column counts use app width and do not guarantee the same fit in every SharePoint panel, so Learn advises host testing.
claims.quote:
The form's NumberOfColumns formula uses the app's width:
If(App.Width < 640, 1, If(App.Width < 900, 2, 3))
These app-width breakpoints don't guarantee how many columns fit inside every SharePoint panel. Check the form in its actual host, not only in Studio.

claims.quote: Preserve the generated actions so the nested form responds to the list's New, View, Edit, Save, and Cancel operations:

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance

claims.quote:

claims.claim: Microsoft has not defined tenant eligibility for the new template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive custom forms template eligibility; site:learn.microsoft.com responsive SharePoint eligible template. Opened sharepoint-form-integration and customize-list-form; read roadmap record. No eligibility criteria were stated.

claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive custom forms template licensing default enabled eligibility environment admin switch; responsive SharePoint template disable. Read roadmap and sharepoint-form-integration: 'where it's enabled for new form creation'; no arrival default is specified.

claims.where: Why it matters: Anyone who creates a new custom form

claims.quote: This article describes the responsive template where it's enabled for new form creation.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Replacing generated formulas based on Parent.NumberOfColumns with fixed values can stop fields reflowing.
claims.quote: Generated data cards use formulas based on Parent.NumberOfColumns for their position and width. Replacing those formulas with fixed values can stop fields from reflowing.

claims.claim: The form's DataSource remains the SharePoint list being customised.
claims.quote: The form's DataSource is the list you customize.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users with at least Read or Restricted View on the linked list inherit access to the customised form.
claims.quote: any user who has at least Read or Restricted View access to the linked SharePoint list inherits access to the form.

claims.claim: Permissions only to specific list items do not confer access to the customised form.
claims.quote: Users who have only been given permissions to specific items in the list don't have access to the customized form.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap and feature documentation describe no new identity, data-access or autonomous-action mechanism.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive custom forms template; read roadmap record and full sharepoint-form-integration article, including DataSource, default actions and user access. They describe layout and existing list integration, not a new identity or autonomous data-access mechanism.

claims.claim: Learn advises against Launch() in SharePointIntegration properties because events can run in the background while the form is not visible.
claims.quote: Don't use imperative functions such as Launch() in SharePointIntegration properties such as OnNew and OnView. These events can run in the background even when the form isn't visible.

claims.claim: Learn states there is currently no automated method in Power Apps to copy a form between environments.
claims.quote: While you can manually copy a form from one environment to another, there's currently no automated method in Power Apps to copy a form from one environment to another.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence specific to the new template's preview or General Availability release is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps responsive SharePoint forms Flexible template preview licensing meter; SharePoint custom forms license standard. Opened sharepoint-form-integration, customize-list-form, pricing-billing-skus and powerapps-licensing-faq. No template-specific licence rule was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The SharePoint forms integration article names no prerequisite licence.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive forms licensing; opened and read full sharepoint-form-integration article, including creation instructions and user-access section. It contains no prerequisite licence statement.

claims.claim: No meter specific to this layout feature is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps responsive SharePoint forms Flexible template preview licensing meter; site:learn.microsoft.com SharePoint form meter Power Apps. Read sharepoint-form-integration and pricing-billing-skus. General Power Apps meters exist; none was assigned to this layout feature.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The general integration overview lists a Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform subscription as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: A subscription to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform.

claims.claim: Some Microsoft 365 licences include limited Power Apps rights intended for Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.
claims.quote: Some Microsoft 365 licenses include limited Power Apps and Power Automate use rights. These use rights are intended for scenarios that use Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.

claims.claim: Standalone premium licensing provides rights beyond the limited Microsoft 365 rights for premium capabilities.
claims.quote:
They don't provide the same rights as standalone premium licenses.
For example, Power Apps Premium and Power Automate Premium provide premium capabilities for licensed users.

claims.claim: Learn advises checking forms at each layout size.
claims.quote: Check long labels, multiline fields, required-field messages, and scrolling at each layout size.

claims.claim: Creating a custom SharePoint form creates a canvas app in the default environment unless a different form environment is designated.
claims.quote: When a maker creates a custom SharePoint form in SharePoint, it creates a canvas app in the default environment. To avoid cluttering the default environment with these apps, create a separate environment to store custom SharePoint forms.

claims.claim: No Power Platform admin center UI path is documented for designating the SharePoint custom form environment.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint custom form environment designate Power Platform admin center UI Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment. Opened powerapps-powershell, manage-default-environment and admin-manage-apps; designation uses PowerShell, not a documented UI setting.

claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment -EnvironmentName '<EnvironmentName>' designates where newly created SharePoint custom forms are saved.
claims.quote:
Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment -EnvironmentName 'EnvironmentName'
This command designates the environment newly created SharePoint custom forms save to, instead of the default environment.

claims.claim: Only tenant admins can call the environment-designation cmdlet.
claims.quote: Modifies which environment Power Platform users save Sharepoint form apps. Only tenant admins can call this command.

claims.claim: Only production environments can be designated for SharePoint custom forms.
claims.quote: Only production environment can be designated for SharePoint custom forms.

claims.claim: Changing the designated environment does not automatically migrate existing forms.
claims.quote: Existing custom forms don't automatically migrate to the newly designated environment.

claims.claim: Deleting the designated environment deletes the custom forms stored in it.
claims.quote: If the designated SharePoint custom form environment is deleted, the custom forms are deleted with it.

claims.claim: Learn's PowerShell guidance specifies the Environment Maker role for creating a form in a designated environment.
claims.quote: The ability for a user to create a custom form in a designated environment requires that user to have the Environment Maker role.

claims.claim: The environment-control documentation covers SharePoint custom forms generally without explicitly naming the new responsive template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint custom form environment designate Power Platform admin center UI. Read designation sections in powerapps-powershell and manage-default-environment and maker-role section in admin-manage-apps; none explicitly names the responsive template.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no setting specifically turning the new starting template on or off or keeping the previous starting template.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com SharePoint responsive template disable; SharePoint responsive custom forms template default enabled admin switch. Read sharepoint-form-integration, powerapps-powershell and search excerpts; no starting-template selection switch was documented.

claims.claim: The SharePoint custom form maker role can restrict makers to creating and editing SharePoint custom forms in a nondefault environment.
claims.quote: it's also possible to limit maker privileges to only be able to create and edit SharePoint custom forms in a nondefault environment.

claims.claim: Distinguishing SharePoint custom form makers from general Environment Makers requires Dataverse in the environment.
claims.quote: The ability to distinguish SharePoint custom form makers from general Environment Makers requires Dataverse in the environment where the privilege is to be changed.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review list access permissions, but that control has no controls-table row.
claims.quote:
Review lists whose forms were customised for Read and Restricted View access, since users with those permissions inherit access to the form.
The only table row is 'Environment where new SharePoint custom forms are saved'.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet beginning 'Review lists whose forms were customised for Read and Restricted View access'; it names a permissions control absent from the table. The existing risk section can retain its access explanation.

controlChecks.governs: Environment where new SharePoint custom forms are saved
